QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_17

question.text: A tax-free bond offers 7.5% interest. For an investor in the 30% tax bracket, what taxable return would be equivalent?

explanation.text: The Logic: Equivalent taxable return = Tax-free return / (1 - Tax rate) = 7.5% / (1 - 0.30) = 7.5% / 0.70 = 10.71%. The Trap: Candidates often multiply 7.5% by 1.30 (getting 9.75%) instead of dividing by (1-0.30). The correct formula inverts the post-tax calculation. Cross-Exam Context: Tax-equivalent yield is crucial for comparing tax-free and taxable instruments. Higher the tax bracket, more attractive tax-free instruments become.
